A wildfire is ripping across the fern flat and an entire mixed herd of iguanodons and hadrosaurs is stampeding through the smoke, heads low, tails streaming, one juvenile hadrosaur clinging to its mother's flank mid-stride.
A herd of brachiosaurs is forming a long procession along a clay ridge, necks swaying in rhythmic unison as they lumber forward, the smallest calf trotting double-speed at the rear just to keep pace.

A dozen hadrosaurs are crowded at a watering hole, heads dipping and lifting in overlapping waves, two youngsters mid-splash fight while adults bump and jostle for the best drinking position at the muddy edge.
A mass stampede of ceratopsians is thundering across an open plain, horns glinting, dust rising, three at the back colliding mid-turn as the herd bends around a fallen tree trunk in a chaotic arc.

A parent ankylosaurus is crouched low over a clutch of tiny speckled eggs, tail club mid-swing and knocking a sneaky oviraptor clean off its feet while a second oviraptor freezes wide-eyed one step behind it.
A mother brachiosaurus is bending her enormous neck all the way to the ground where three hatchlings are tumbling over each other to reach the leafy bundle she is lowering, one latched on mid-wobble.

Two juvenile pachycephalosauruses are headbutting each other in a clumsy practice bout, both reeling back dazed with tiny stars implied, while a third watches from the side looking deeply unimpressed.

A hapless ankylosaur has waded too deep into the tar pit and is thrashing its front legs in slow syrup while a sauropod stretches its neck as far as it can reach and a stegosaurus bites down on the sauropod's tail to act as an anchor.

A rotund iguanodon has gotten its wide hips jammed between two clay boulders mid-escape and is wiggling frantically while two velociraptors arrive at the scene, stare at it, then look at each other completely baffled.

A pteranodon has swooped too low over the watering hole and is tangled in a hadrosaur's bony crest, both flapping and honking in opposite directions while a second hadrosaur nearby backs away with visible concern.

A meteor blazes a bright orange streak across the sky and every dinosaur in the valley — triceratops, diplodocus, and a pair of raptors mid-hunt — has frozen completely, every neck craned upward, every eye locked on the fireball.

A strange glowing aurora has lit the night sky purple and green and a scattered group of sauropods, a nodosaurus, and two pterosaurs perched on a rock are all tilted skyward motionless, bathed in the eerie reflected glow.

A long column of parasaurolophus is winding through a misty fern flat in single file, crests raised and calling in overlapping honks that ripple down the line, the rearmost pair glancing nervously back over their shoulders.

Three pterosaurs are spiraling upward on a clay thermal column, wings wide and tilted, riding in a lazy rising circle while two more below stretch their wings and prepare to launch off a rocky ledge into the updraft.

A pod of diplodocuses is stretched out on a sunny clay flat, necks extended and eyes half-closed, while two small compsognathus pick bugs off the nearest one's back and it barely twitches an ear in acknowledgment.

Two crocodilians are sprawled flat and motionless in shallow mud, soaking up reflected heat, while a small nodosaurus inches in sideways between them to claim a warm patch, freezing every time one of them shifts.

A ceratosaurus and an acrocanthosaurus are locked in a biting grapple on a riverbank, jaws clamped on each other's necks and claws churning the clay, tails lashing wide arcs that send two unlucky gallimimus scrambling for the tree line.
A juvenile T-rex is sprinting flat-out after a zigzagging iguanodon across a fern flat, jaws snapping inches from its tail, while two hadrosaurs nearby wheel and bolt in the opposite direction.
Three velociraptors are fanning out in a pincer formation around a panicked pachycephalosaurus, the center raptor mid-leap, the flankers crouched low with claws splayed, closing the trap.
A spinosaurus is wading chest-deep into a clay river, lunging at a thrashing prehistoric fish, while two frightened plesiosaurs surface-dive away in opposing arcs of white foam.
A triceratops and a styracosaurus are locked horn-to-horn in a shoving match, feet gouging the earth, both leaning at a forty-five-degree angle, neither giving an inch of ground.
Two allosauruses are circling a lone stegosaurus in tightening loops, heads low and swaying, while the stegosaurus pivots slowly, spike-tail raised and trembling, tracking both threats at once.
A T-rex and a spinosaurus are face-to-chest on a narrow clay ridge, both rearing back mid-roar, tails lashing for balance, every smaller dinosaur in the valley sprinting away below them.

A volcano is mid-blast and four dinosaurs — a brachiosaurus, two triceratops, and a single gallimimus — are stampeding across a lava-cracked plain, the gallimimus already three lengths ahead of the rest.
A flash flood is churning through a fern canyon and a herd of mixed hadrosaurs is scrambling up the clay banks, several half-submerged, legs churning, necks stretched high above the rushing water.

A wildfire is sweeping across the diorama's edge and an ankylosaur, two parasaurolophus, and a frightened juvenile brachiosaurus are all fleeing in the same direction, silhouetted against an orange glow.
A long migration line of brachiosauruses is winding single-file along a clay ridge, the lead adult stretching its neck around a bend, the rearmost juvenile stumbling to catch up on stubby legs.

A procession of hadrosaurs is crossing a shallow fern flat in a rolling, nose-to-tail column, the adults honking with crests flushed bright, the juveniles trotting between the adults' feet in a chaotic weave.
A herd of pachycephalosauruses is pushing and jostling at a narrow clay watering hole, two fighting for the best spot, one getting bumped sideways mid-sip, water splashing in every direction.

A parent ankylosaurus is hunched wide over a nest of speckled eggs, tail-club raised and quivering, while three approaching oviraptors freeze in a crouch, eyeing the eggs from a very cautious distance.

Two tiny hatchling raptors are tumbling beak-over-tail outside their broken clay eggshells, a third is halfway out mid-wobble, and the exhausted parent crouches over all three with open wings trembling.
A mother brachiosaurus is leaning her colossal neck down to nudge a fallen juvenile back onto its feet, while a second juvenile uses the opportunity to steal a mouthful of fern from mom's mouth.

An ankylosaur has blundered into a tar pit up to its armpits, rear legs bicycling helplessly in the air, while two nearby sauropods stretch their necks toward it in an accidental, wobbling rescue chain.

A rotund stegosaurus has slipped off a clay log crossing a shallow creek, landed belly-up in the water, legs waving at the sky, while three pterosaurs on the bank stare down at it in apparent disbelief.

A hapless gallimimus has run full-speed into a clay boulder, bounced onto its back, and is scrambling upright while the raptor that was chasing it slides past on all fours, equally confused by the sudden stop.

A whole herd of iguanodons is grazing in a wide arc across the clay plain, several pulling at fern fronds mid-bite, one calf chasing its mother's tail, the outermost adults scanning the treeline with raised heads.

A pod of sleeping brachiosauruses is curled neck-over-neck in a loose circle, the smallest pressed into the center, while a tiny compsognathus tiptoes between two enormous heads, helping itself to scraps.

Three crocodilians are sprawled flat on a sun-warmed clay bank, jaws open at full gape, while two ankylosaurs wade into the shallows beside them, blissfully ignoring the crocodilians who crack one eye each.

Every dinosaur in the diorama — hadrosaurs, raptors, even a mid-roar T-rex — has frozen in place craning upward at a blazing green meteor streak crossing the sky, total silence implied across the whole herd.
A fleet of pterosaurs is riding a thermal column in a wide rising spiral, wings locked, tips curling upward, while the ground herd below grinds to a halt and tilts every head skyward to watch.

A ceratosaurus and a carnotaurus are biting and shoving in a full jaw-lock grapple, rolling sideways through a fern thicket, while two fleeing diplodocuses send the thicket exploding in all directions.

A pack of raptors is mid-sprint through a stand of tall ferns in pursuit of a gallimimus, the lead raptor's claws raking the gallimimus's tail, two raptors leaping over fallen logs, the third slipping on wet clay.
